Home / Compliance

Documentation, verification and how we stay compliant

A shipment that cannot be documented cannot be cleared, financed or insured. This is what we prepare, and the rules we work within.

The document set

Six groups of documents on every shipment

Exact contents depend on the commodity, origin and destination.

1Certificate of origin
Issued through the relevant chamber of commerce or authority. Used for tariff, sanctions and import compliance.
2Independent inspection and assay
Quality, quantity and composition reports from an independent surveyor or laboratory, such as assay for minerals, shore-tank and ship reports for oil, or gemmological reports for stones. The buyer chooses the inspector.
3Government permits and payments
Export licences, royalty and duty receipts, radiation or hazardous-goods clearance where required, and any foreign-exchange or central bank approvals.
4Provenance and chain of custody
Records of every transfer from origin to loading, supporting OECD-aligned due diligence, Kimberley Process requirements for rough diamonds, and sanctions screening.
5Commercial and banking documents
Commercial invoice, packing list, weight and quantity certificates, formatted to meet letter-of-credit presentation requirements agreed with your bank.
6Transport and insurance
Bill of lading or air waybill, charter party where applicable, and cargo insurance arranged on the terms agreed in the contract.
Our rules

How we work

Know your counterparty

We verify the identity and ownership of the parties we deal with and screen them against sanctions lists before any contract proceeds.

Verify before release

Your appointed inspector may sample material before processing, at sealing or loading, and at discharge.

Confidentiality and non-circumvention

We sign a mutual non-circumvention and non-disclosure agreement on request. We do not approach your end buyer without your written authority.

We decline mandates where origin, ownership, licensing or sanctions status cannot be established to our satisfaction. [Add your AML / KYC policy summary and compliance officer contact here.]

Three checkpoints

Inspection access

Buyers and their appointed surveyors are welcome at each stage.

  1. Before processingSample raw ore, rough parcels or shore-tank stock to set a baseline.
  2. At sealing or loadingIndependent sampling, serialised seals and the binding quality and quantity report.
  3. At dischargeReconciliation at the destination port, airport or vault before final payment.

Need our confidentiality agreement first?

Tick the confidentiality option on the enquiry form and we will send the agreement before you share end-buyer details.
